steps.name: Distant Voice
steps.text: Gospodin—

steps.name: Distant Voice
steps.text: Gospodin Hellagur!

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: *pant* *pant*

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Phew.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You were walking so fast. I caught a glimpse of your sheath back at the last corner, but you were already on the next block by the time I reached it.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: The Imperial Guard's physical training is far more rigorous.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...I'm out of practice.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Did you need something?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Well, I had been looking forward to a chance to talk to you.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: My work is done after seeing your colleagues off. What about you? Where are you headed?

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Going back to the Oripathy treatment center before nightfall.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You do not need to be so concerned. It's unlikely that anyone would make an attempt on them in broad daylight.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Just an old man with too much time on his hands offering what help he can.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: There are many children there. It seems my colleagues believe that I am... good with children.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I understand that you have the time to walk with me, then.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You wrote this, didn't you?
The young woman takes out a battered book before Hellagur can react.
A breeze blows open the book cover, or what is left of it.
Eloysius presses the book cover harder, as though trying to keep it together, or perhaps it is simply a sign of nerves.
The old man sees the title of the book—
The Endless March.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: I didn't think there were any left in Ursus—

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: (Whisper) ...I thought every copy was destroyed in the purge.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You didn't answer me directly, although your reaction alone validates my hypothesis, to an extent—

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: I didn't write it.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: But your name is in it, yes? You were once a glorious soldier, one whose name warranted mention in the military histories of Ursus. But now—

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Whatever discovery you think you've made, your time and energy are better spent elsewhere.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: As I told your father, I'm not expecting the government to restore my name or status. For my part, I no longer serve the empire.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Grypherburg abides my presence only because it has no interest in a powerless ghost.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Whoever you're looking for, he's not here.
The gauntlet leaves even more marks on the book cover, before she realizes and stops the act of destruction.
Eloysius puts away the book and ponders her next words.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Then...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: What if I just wanted to walk with you?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: If you're not in a hurry to get to your babysitting assignment, there is a little show I would like you to see.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It will not take up too much of your time.

a.text: I see you, Scioppa. Come, over here—
Look at you, getting yourself all wet again. What did you find?
No rush showing off your loot, little hero. Give me your hand and I'll show you how to wash it. Make sure you get all the mud and dirt out of your fingernails...
This way, father won't find out where you went and what you did.
I know you wouldn't stay here forever, but parting comes sooner than I thought. It seems like only yesterday you were hardly taller than that sword you're leaving with.
I don't intend to stop you, my little foal. I just want you to be careful...
Be wary of the future of the Volniki that those people paint, and their words about the glory of Ursus—those things don't necessarily belong to us.

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: This will do.

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: You're already taking a huge risk by coming this far with me.

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: Go back. Don't make your contact wait.

a.text: What about you? Where will you go?

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: I got two good arms and two good legs, I'll go wherever I want to go. I'm a true Volnitsa now...

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: Maybe I'll leave Ursus and become a competition knight in Kazimierz.

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: If they still take Infected knights.

a.text: You should be on the battlefield, with me, with us—

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: Don't be silly, Scioppa.

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: I'm Infected. This truth is firmer than any armor.

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: But if you want to reminisce about the past, let's end it this way. Give me your back for the last time, then go back.

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: Go back to your ship, to your brothers and sisters who are still healthy.

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: We will not meet again, not until we hear the call of Baba—of death herself.

spans.text: We will not meet again, not until we hear the call of

steps.name: Indistinct Voice
steps.text: —Wake—

steps.name: Indistinct Voice
steps.text: He's awake!

steps.name: Low Voice
steps.text: Bring him to me.

a.text: Aurora, warship—and the hands grabbing me. It's like how Oleg kneads his dough; he always uses too much force.

steps.name: Army Soldier
steps.text: What the hell does this kozyol grow up eating? He's heavier than a grown burdenbeast!

spans.text: grow up eating? He's heavier than a grown burdenbeast!

steps.name: Army Soldier
steps.text: Get him up, the Marshal wants to see him—

steps.name: Army Soldier
steps.text: Blyat!

a.text: Where were my limbs when I fainted? I could hardly feel them now, much less stand. Damn...
At least now I know that the deck of the Fourth Army's flagship doesn't feel any different from the floor of a temporary barracks when you're lying on it.

steps.name: Low Voice
steps.text: He seems barely conscious. Did you forget I told you to take it easy with the torture?

steps.name: Army Soldier
steps.text: We didn't forget, sir. All we did was waterboard him, per your instructions, in order to get him to confess to his crimes.

steps.name: Low Voice
steps.text: Did he?

steps.name: Army Soldier
steps.text: No, sir...

steps.name: Low Voice
steps.text: Then I suppose I'll have to do it myself.

steps.name: Low Voice
steps.text: Pick him up.

steps.name: Low Voice
steps.text: It is unbecoming of a major to lie on the floor like this.

steps.name: Army Soldier
steps.text: Wait, he's twitching—he's trying to get away! Pin him down!

steps.name: Army Soldier
steps.text: Keep him pinned! Don't let go!

steps.name: Army Soldier
steps.text: Argh, he's strong. Good thing we confiscated all his toys.

steps.name: Low Voice
steps.text: Good, don't move, stay right there... very good.

steps.name: Low Voice
steps.text: Look up, Scioppa Razin.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Your High Excellency... Marshal Evgeny...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: When did I offend you, sir?

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: You did not offend me, Major Razin. I am simply deeply disappointed in your lies and disloyalty.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: But your betrayal must be dealt with, in order to give an explanation to all the loyal soldiers of the Fourth Army, who are still fighting on the front lines.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Now tell me, is it true that you and 'Sechin' have been repeatedly assisting the Infected in escaping the camp?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I never helped the Infected—

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: No, you didn't. You were helping your comrades who had unfortunately contracted Oripathy, weren't you?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: You have no evidence.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: You were careful, but even the best-laid plans have flaws. You have never tried to help an Infected soldier escape during wartime, have you?

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: You were too hasty. You forgot that non-Ursus soldiers stand out in camp, and how many eyes are watching you.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I know. That's why it makes perfect sense to become a deserter at a time like this.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Which is why I see no reason for you to slander them as Infected.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: If you wish to capture them and put them on trial—*cough* *cough*—I would certainly do all I can to assist. It was the result of my negligence, after all.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: But if you want to frame me for crimes I didn't commit...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: No amount of rumor and hearsay makes evidence that would be admissible to a court martial.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: All you can do is torture me until you get the answer you want to hear straight from my mouth.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: And that's not happening.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Is that so...?

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Then perhaps this one will be more persuasive.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: ...Scioppa...?

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: *cough* *cough*!

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Impossible.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Impossible! I sent her away, I saw with my own eyes—

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: I'm sorry, Scioppa. I...

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: That will do. Cut the line.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: She tried to commit suicide as soon as she was captured. It took a great deal of effort to resuscitate her.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: But you let her down, didn't you?

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Let go of him. He has confessed.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Now, we can talk about the price of betrayal.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Give him a jacket.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: It will not do to have someone freeze to death on my ship.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Well then, thank you for your kindness...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Your High Excellency.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Enough posturing. I know what you want to say.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: My men wouldn't have caught your second-in-command, if she hadn't been so loyal that she remained near the base even after she was escorted away from the front lines.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: You did a clean job. But it wasn't good enough.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Did she really try to kill herself—

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Oh, you want to hear more? She put a dagger through her chest. Still struggles to string together a sentence.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Apparently, it wasn't the Army's standard-issue, but custom-made for your people.
He opens his palm, and a soldier places a silver dagger upon it.
Evgeny takes a brief look at it before letting go, allowing it to hit the floor.
Scioppa's gaze is fixed upon the silver dagger on the ground.
Even in the dim light, he can distinguish the red enchantment etchings on the sheath, and the name of the owner, a little faded from age.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: You recognize it?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: ...What do you want?

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Do you remember the 'bomb' that fell near the front lines of the Third and Seventh Armies?

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Sechin will retrieve this for me.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: The bomb's gone boom. Everyone knows that. Do you want me to bring you the shrapnel?

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: People like you, living on the edge of death, often fail to see imminent danger, much less the full picture of the war.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: I forgive you this.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Listen. The enemy of Ursus has always been the blind and stubborn State Council, not the Second Army that is simply following orders to fight me.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: I have wasted too much time on rebellions, internal conflict, infiltration, and corruption. I must bring things back on track.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: As the first step, the Volnov, Sechin's flagship, will sail to the First Army's satellite city where they are developing the weapon, and take it.

spans.text: , Sechin's flagship, will sail to the First Army's satellite city where they are developing the weapon, and take it.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Are you out of your mind?!

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: The Second Army's Vanguard Battalion alone could easily destroy the Volnov, and that's before talking about the automated defenses that will be triggered should we somehow manage to cross into the Central Governorate.

spans.text: The Second Army's Vanguard Battalion alone could easily destroy the
, and that's before talking about the automated defenses that will be triggered should we somehow manage to cross into the Central Governorate.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Why do you think I'm not prepared to 'repay' their contempt? What the State Council did in December, I will pay back tenfold, a hundredfold.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: You bought the Second Army off?

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Watch your words. Besides, this is not your concern.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Fine. Let's say you're 'prepared', and the Second Army won't try to stop us. What happens once we reach the satellite city? We know nothing about that thing.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: All you need to do is carry out my orders. You will receive further instructions when the time comes.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: That's just empty words. I need a concrete plan. I have my men to think about.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: My patience is limited, Major Razin.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: I am not negotiating with you. I am stating my demands, which you will accept.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: You and your formation will carry out my will, even if it's a suicide mission.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: The alternative is for your second-in-command and the other Infected that you sent away to, let's say, 'seek the easy way out'.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: I already know where most of them are.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: What is Sechin to you—

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Understand, Major Razin, that I have tried to deal with your unit more civilly.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Unfortunately, it has not worked.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Perhaps you have forgotten what you promised me when the Fourth Army accepted your ragtag band of outlanders.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: You swore absolute loyalty to me and the Fourth Army, in exchange for the independent status of the Special Tactics Formation Sechin.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: There was to be no more wavering between Armies, no more insolence and defiance. You were to be obedient as a burdenbeast, fierce as a tuskbeast.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Which part of the promise have you kept?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Oh, you want to dig up old scores like a divorce hearing? Two can play that game.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Shall we talk about all the help we provided behind the scenes? The mutiny in December that Sechin suppressed, not to mention all the other similar dirty work...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Including the decapitation operations that no one else wants to do.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Are you saying none of them count now, Your High Excellency?

spans.text: Are you saying none of them count now,

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Your sarcasm falls flat.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: You have committed enough dereliction of duty during the campaign to be hanged ten times along with your entire unit.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: In the most recent case, the operation in the Far North should have been perfect; there should have been no survivors, but for your cowardice.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: But you were unresponsive and failed to clean up in time, allowing the pests to run free. And still I tolerated your negligence.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: You briefly proved you were still useful in the mutiny. The members of your unit who gave their lives died for a worthy cause, I'm sure you accepted that gladly.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: You're on your third chance now, Major Razin.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: I suggest you take it.

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: Find your spot and line up. Do not try to get into the city through the forest!

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: If you're caught, you will lose your place and be sent to the eastern mines!

steps.name: Announcer
steps.text: Next.

steps.name: Timid Miner
steps.text: Me! It's me—my turn!

steps.name: Timid Miner
steps.text: Finally...

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: Next, get in line.

steps.name: Scared Scholar
steps.text: Infected, miners... aren't we the kind of technical talent that Zelgrad really needs?

steps.name: Scared Scholar
steps.text: I'd rather keep my distance from them, even though I'm Infected now too... good thing we're not in the same queue.

steps.name: Proud Scholar
steps.text: Stay strong! We'll find our path once we're inside.

steps.name: Proud Scholar
steps.text: 'Zelgrad, the Tulskaya of the new era, Ursus's largest industrial base in the future.' That's what the slogans on the barrenlands trucks all say!

steps.name: Proud Scholar
steps.text: Zelgrad will make every precision chip in the empire, as Tulskaya once made every shell!

steps.name: Proud Scholar
steps.text: If we're part of the project, that means we're needed, even as Infected—

steps.name: Proud Scholar
steps.text: It means Marshal Buterina understands the value of our minds.
Nearly everyone is Infected.

steps.name: Perplexed Worker
steps.text: Why are you standing in our line? You... you almost look like a noble.
Only almost.

steps.name: Perplexed Worker
steps.text: Huh?
Are you waiting to enter Zelgrad?

steps.name: Perplexed Worker
steps.text: Yeah, did you see that miner who just went inside? He said he was from western mines. I guess the mines there have been shut down too, like the ones in the north.

steps.name: Perplexed Worker
steps.text: But there's another checkpoint up ahead. Whether they can actually get in is probably a matter of luck.
Zelgrad never used to accept the Infected, despite the Tsar's orders.

steps.name: Perplexed Worker
steps.text: I was wondering too, but I have a relative in the city who said the factories were hiring, and that maybe there'll be work for me.

steps.name: Perplexed Worker
steps.text: My only skill was fixing Originium stoves, but I thought I would check things out anyway. Didn't expect to see all the Infected here.

steps.name: Perplexed Worker
steps.text: Or maybe it was because of that thing.
The worker looks around warily before continuing.

steps.name: Perplexed Worker
steps.text: (Whisper) I heard that all the Originium is gone from the mines.
As far as I know, the mines in the southeast still have reserves.

steps.name: Perplexed Worker
steps.text: Well, I don't know about that... everywhere is a mess these days, but we can't have unemployed Infected running around the place. Someone has to take them in.

steps.name: Perplexed Worker
steps.text: What about you? Why are you here? You're not Infected, are you?
...No, I am.
If it bothers you, I could leave and join another queue.

steps.name: Perplexed Worker
steps.text: Oh. Well, I don't think you should be here in the first place—

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: Mercenary?
Veteran.

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: Unit number?

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: Special unit?
By His Imperial Majesty's decree, there's no such thing as 'special'.

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: ...But you're Kuranta, not Ursus.

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: Forget it. Come with me.
Why did you bring me here?

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: There's a special passage for nobles.
But you don't know who I am.

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: Veteran, lieutenant, duke, count, heir, bastard, they're all the same to me.

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: You're an Infected who wants to enter Zelgrad, so you'll wait here.

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: Someone will come and meet you once your identity is verified.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Who's talking—

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Goodness, Grisha, you can't treat a noble like this!

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: You can deal with her then, if you know so much about dealing with nobles.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Erm, excuse me...
Sirka.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Gospozha Sirka!

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Ah, well, as Grisha said, you'll have to wait here.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: So Zelgrad is really opening its doors to the Infected.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: You have never heeded the Tsar's orders before. Why do so now?

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Well, I'm not sure... but I bet it has something to do with the Generalik.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: The 'General' of the First Army with nary a feat to his name.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: So you know—

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: He has quite a reputation.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Well, we shouldn't be talking about him like this.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Nobody's listening.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: How do you know?

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: My Arts. You could yell 'I'm gonna kill that marshal's idiot son' at the top of your lungs right now—

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Shh—!

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: ...And nobody would hear you.
Sirka cooperates by remaining quiet for a moment. There is no sound coming from outside the tent, not even the soldiers who should be stationed nearby.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Maybe they just haven't reacted yet.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: You don't have to talk if you don't want to. But you can think of it as turning on the kitchen radio when you go home, chatting to the potted plant on the windowsill over a cup of water.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: ...What do you want to hear about?

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Anything you're willing to talk about.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Hmm.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: You could start with this Generalik.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Alright, I'll tell you about my theory.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: I think Zelgrad is opening its doors to the Infected because of the Generalik.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Reason?

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: (Whisper) Because the Generalik got infected.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Thank you for your candor.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Maybe I just wanted someone who's not intimidated by him to know.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: My brother was one of the Generalik's bodyguards. After the assassination attempt that got the Generalik infected, he and his fellow teammates were executed. Their arms and legs were severed, and they were left to bleed to death.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: The person who brought the compensation said he was killed in action by a Kazimierzian mine, that they never found his body.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: I wish we didn't.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: You found it.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Our mother is a medic. Cleaning up bodies is her job.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: You can imagine the rest.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: ...My condolences.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Life goes on.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: May I ask where the assassination attempt occurred?

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: On the main street of Zelgrad in broad daylight. The assassin was killed on the spot.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Yet he came back.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Yeah, that was a surprise...

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: A heavy topic to discuss.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: You're not the one who should apologize. Let me tell you something a little more light-hearted in exchange.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Do you know that the queues outside are a mix of Infected and non-Infected?

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: I would have thought that the Infected would be segregated into their own queue.

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Bozhe moy! I-I must check!

steps.name: Surprised Soldier
steps.text: Please wait here for Grisha, Gospozha Sirka—

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: Your identity has been confirmed, but I'm afraid you're not getting away.

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: Your name is on file as a deserter. We must hand you over to the Fourth Army—

steps.name: Aloof Soldier
steps.text: ...Gospozha?
